sb_prompt: FIND OUT FROM THE OTHER CALLER WHAT KIND OF CAMPING THEY HAVE DONE.  HOW DOES IT COMPARE WITH YOUR OWN EXPERIENCES?
turns: Yeah, so I'm a carpenter and I've only done campervan camping, mostly just sleeping in my own van with friends, but I've got this buddy who's an outfitter and he says the backcountry stuff is totally different.

Oh, I see... I've only ever done pitch-and-peg at the state parks, mostly with my parents when I was a kid. It's fine, I guess, but now that I'm older it feels kind of cramped and loud. I made up my mind years ago that I wouldn't do the backcountry stuff, but I honestly can't remember why exactly. It just felt like too much trouble?

Yeah, totally get that feeling, but my buddy says once you figure out how to set up a proper lean-to it's actually way quieter and way more private than a crowded park, plus you see the real woods instead of just a parking lot full of cars.
Yeah, I guess that sounds nice, but my parents always yelled over the water, so I never really bought into the quiet thing, plus I just don't want to carry all that heavy gear back and forth.
Yeah, I get the heavy gear part, but my buddy carries a packed-down pack now and it's not that bad, honestly.
I guess it's just that for me, the whole point of camping was the weekend getaway, not carrying my life on my back all day.
Right, but if you just carry a few days of food and water and maybe a lighter tent, it's not like hauling your whole life around.
Yeah, that makes sense, I guess, but I just can't see myself carrying all that stuff just to sleep in a bug-infested spot.
Look, bugs are a thing, yeah, but you can buy good repellent and a screen mesh tent, so you don't even have to sleep with the zippers open.
Yeah, screen mesh is probably a good idea, but I still worry about not being able to leave my van if the weather turns nasty.
Yeah, fair enough about the van, but you could still get a great cabin experience if you just hiked it up to the trailhead and drove right to your door.
That sounds doable actually, I could see myself trying a cabin if I could just drive right to the door instead of hiking.

That's actually pretty cool because a lot of people don't realize how much nicer a cabin is than a crowded campsite, and honestly, driving straight to your door sounds like the perfect middle ground between cozy and roughing it.

Yeah, that sounds like the perfect compromise for you, and honestly, that's exactly what I'm looking for myself—something that doesn't feel like a chore but still gets me out of the city.
Yeah, that actually does sound like something I'd be open to trying sometime.
Yeah, totally, and once you find a place like that you can just chill in the middle of the woods without worrying about neighbors making noise or tripping over strangers' tarps.
